title: When the Choir Burns
premise: In the memoryless valley of Hallowmere, Quentin Vane survives by stealing recollections from travelers who cross its borders, trading them for bread and silence. When the crown's witch-hunters breach the valley hunting 'the gift,' they drag Quentin and their sworn protector, Wren, into a capital where the king has been hollowed out by a crown that eats memories — the same crown whose stolen memories Quentin carries without knowing it. To unbind the king, Quentin must surrender every memory they have ever stolen, including the ones that made them who they are, while Wren must choose between loyalty to the order that raised them and the truth about what the hunt really serves. In the burning choir of the cathedral, Quentin empties themselves to free the king, and Wren carries what remains — a person with no past, loved into a new one.
about_author: Silas Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging the letters of the disappeared and now writes fantasy about what people carry when everything else is taken. They live near water, keep no diary, and claim this is a professional decision.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin steals a traveler's memory of a daughter's wedding, trading it at the market, and we see how they hoard the stolen pasts in jars like fireflies. Establishes the valley's magic-dead quiet and Quentin's loneliness. Beat: contentment with an undertow of hunger.

chapters.title: Wren at the Border
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, a warden sworn to guard the valley's edge, catches Quentin smuggling memories out and lets them go — the third such mercy. Their history as reluctant partners surfaces. Beat: tenderness disguised as duty.

chapters.title: What the Traveler Carried
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Among a dying traveler's memories, Quentin finds fragments of a coronation — and inside it, something that looks back at them through the memory itself. The jar shatters on its own. Beat: first dread.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Mill
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Crown riders post a decree: all bearers of the gift are to be surrendered or burned. The valley's elders vote to give up any stranger among them. Beat: the community's safety curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: The Gift They Never Named
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin admits to Wren that their theft is the gift — memory-craft, the rarest kind. Wren realizes their own oath-marks are a weaker strain of the same magic. Beat: intimacy through shared danger.

chapters.title: Hounds of the Hunt
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Witch-hunters cross the border — impossible, since magic cannot follow — led by Inquisitor Hale, who wears a collar that lets him carry magic like a weapon. Beat: the sanctuary's rules breaking.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The hunt seizes Quentin; Wren's intervention fails and they are both dragged from the valley in iron wagons lined with memory-leeching salt. Quentin's hoard is confiscated — except the coronation fragments, which hide inside them. Beat: helplessness, and a strange relief at leaving.

chapters.title: The City of Bells
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The capital gleams and rots; every bell tower is a memory-ward. Quentin glimpses the king at a distance and recognizes his face from the stolen coronation — but wrong, smoothed, vacant. Beat: recognition and vertigo.

chapters.title: Cells and Confessions
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Imprisoned separately, Wren is offered freedom in exchange for testimony against Quentin. Wren learns the hunt's true purpose: not to destroy the gift, but to find someone who can unbind the king. Beat: loyalty tested with a lie.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Brought before the court, Quentin touches the king's hand in ceremony and the coronation memories flare: the crown is a parasite, a hunger that ate the king's past and now rules through him. It notices Quentin noticing. Beat: terror of being seen.

chapters.title: Hale's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Inquisitor Hale reveals he was once a bearer himself, collared and emptied, and offers Wren the same choice he made: serve, and keep a self; refuse, and be burned. Beat: the seduction of survival.

chapters.title: Escape Through the Choir
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin steals a memory from a guard — the layout of the undercroft — and escapes into the cathedral's abandoned choir, where the acoustics hold every voice that ever sang there. Wren finds them there. Beat: reunion as relief and accusation.

chapters.title: What Wren Chose
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confesses they nearly took Hale's bargain and didn't — and that their warden oath was designed by the crown to find bearers, meaning they were the hunt's key all along. Quentin's trust fractures. Beat: love wounded by truth.

chapters.title: The Archive of Stolen Things
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In the crown's vault, Quentin finds their confiscated jars — and centuries of other bearers' hoards, the raw material the parasite feeds on. They understand the king is not the only one it wears. Beat: the scale of the horror revealed.

chapters.title: A Kingdom with No Yesterday
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The kingdom's people are forgetting in waves — names, debts, grievances — as the crown feeds wider. Wren and Quentin see that unbinding the king means giving the parasite a feast large enough to kill it. Beat: grim clarity.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In the choir, Quentin learns the rite from a memory of the last bearer who tried — a memory ending mid-scream. The rite requires a bearer to pour every stolen memory into the parasite at once. Beat: resolve forming over fear.

chapters.title: Hale's Last Collar
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Hale, hollowed to the collar, chooses at the end to open the vault doors for them, buying their passage with what's left of him. Beat: an enemy's redemption, small and costly.

chapters.title: The Burning Choir
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Climax. Before king and court and the parasite's full attention, Quentin sings the rite through the choir's acoustics, pouring in the coronation, the valley, the travelers, their own childhood. The parasite gorges and tears; the crown cracks; the king wakes weeping. Beat: self-annihilation as triumph.

chapters.title: Empty
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Quentin survives but remembers nothing — not the valley, not the thefts, not Wren. The freed king, remembering everything the crown took, offers Quentin restoration from the vault's hoards. Beat: grief without a mourner's name for it.

chapters.title: The Choice of a Self
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Offered their stolen past back, Quentin instead chooses a few small memories — a jar, a border, a hand — and lets the rest go to the kingdom's forgetting. Beat: identity as something made, not recovered.

chapters.title: Return to Hallowmere
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren walks Quentin home across the border, renouncing the oath-marks that made them the hunt's key. The valley receives a stranger gently. Beat: quiet, earned peace.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Shared POV, alternating. In the valley, Quentin begins stealing memories again — only ones freely given now, gifts instead of thefts — while Wren teaches them who they were and who they might be. The crown's fall is a rumor at the border. Beat: love as inheritance, chosen anew each day.
